title: Ivo and the Weather
premise: Ulyana Quintana, a piano tuner in a fading coastal town, discovers a box of undelivered letters behind her late grandmother's wardrobe — letters addressed to a man named Ivo, who vanished decades ago after a fire that the town blamed on him. As she tunes pianos from house to house, she pieces together the truth: Ivo was innocent, and the letters' silence protected the guilty. When she finds Ivo alive but dying in a care home two towns over, she must choose between the loyalty that kept her family's secret and the justice of saying his name aloud. The book ends with Ulyana reading every letter to Ivo at last, then publishing them — trading her family's careful silence for a truth that costs her everything except herself.
about_author: Mirabel Quintana is the pen name of a former piano restorer who spent fifteen years listening to old instruments tell on their owners. She writes about inheritance, sound, and the things families file away instead of forgiving.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Clearing her grandmother's house after the funeral, Ulyana tunes the old upright one last time and hears, through the radiators and floorboards, how grief lives in a building. Behind the wardrobe she finds a shoebox: forty-one sealed letters, all addressed to Ivo Weather, none ever posted. Emotional beat: the shock of realizing the woman she loved most curated a lifelong silence.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, interwoven with the letters themselves. Reading them in order, she reconstructs 1974: the warehouse fire, Ivo's flight, and her grandmother's complicity in shielding the true arsonist — Ulyana's grandfather. Neighbors still repeat the old story when she makes tuning rounds, and she begins lying by omission to protect the dead. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into complicity as she inherits the lie.

chapters.title: Ivo
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A misfiled pension record leads her to Ivo Weather, ninety-one, alive in a care home under a borrowed name. He recognizes the grandmother's handwriting before he recognizes anything else. He refuses absolution but asks for the letters — read aloud, not handed over. Emotional beat: the climax, as Ulyana reads all forty-one letters in one afternoon while Ivo drifts between presence and sleep, finally witnessed.

chapters.title: Tuning Fork
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, weeks later. Ivo has died; the town has learned the truth because Ulyana published the letters against her mother's pleas. Some doors close to her; others open for the first time. In the emptied grandmother's house, she tunes the upright and plays it loud with the windows open. Emotional beat: resolution — justice outside the law, identity claimed through truth, and goodbye said properly, out loud.
